## 2. Offload mechanisms

### 2.1 Memory hierarchy (what lives where)

- **GPU:** all non-expert weights stay resident. The remaining VRAM is split between one global expert slot cache (shared by every layer, slot = (layer, expert)) and KV (paper section 4; `engine/cache_budget.py:48-95`).
- **Host RAM:** the full expert pool, as per-layer `[num_experts, ...]` banks per bank role (`moe/offload_cache.py:292-365`). Host banks are pinned+mapped so the GPU can dereference them.
- **NVMe:** two uses only:
  - (a) load time: an O_DIRECT parallel read of experts into host banks;
  - (b) the **PLE disk row store** at serve time.
- **Experts never page from NVMe at runtime.** There is no third expert tier. Experts must fit in host RAM, or be LOCKED/PAGEABLE for CPU-only decode (`moe/host_banks.py:43-52`).

### 2.2 Decode, `--moe-strategy offload` (fetch misses over PCIe)

`docs/models.md:38-47`; `layers/moe.py:257-293`.

1. **`ensure_experts`** runs flashlib `lru_ensure` on device (`moe/offload_kernels.py:19-40`).
   - It dedups the routed ids, classifies hits and misses, and picks victims by `argmin(usage)` (timestamp LRU over the global slot pool).
   - It writes `evict_slots`, `src_indices` and `num_indices`, and rewrites `topk_ids` to slot ids in place.
   - It is fully device-side and fixed-shape, so it is **CUDA-graph capturable**. Only `lru` exists as a policy (`offload_cache.py:149-150`).
2. **`copy_missing`** uses `fast_index_copy_multi_jit` (`offload_cache.py:1011-1053`; `kernel/fast_index_copy.py:153-185`).
   - This is **not cudaMemcpy**. It is an SM-driven zero-copy gather kernel: GPU threads load 16 B vectors straight from the mapped pinned host banks (`ld.global.L1::no_allocate`) and store with `st.global.wt` into the slot cache (`kernel/csrc/jit/fast_index_copy.cuh:43-106, 510-560`).
   - One launch covers all banks of a layer.
   - The miss count is read on device (`num_indices`), so the copy size is dynamic inside a static graph.
   - Tuning note: about 4096 threads per bank saturates PCIe; the default is 8x1024 per bank. The docstring quotes ~31 GB/s measured (`fast_index_copy.py:166-173`).
3. **Expert GEMM** runs over the whole slot cache with slot ids (`layers/moe.py:282-293`).

Other behavior:

- **Cache sizing.** `--moe-cache-auto` is the default for offload strategies. `plan_cache_budget` is MoE-first:
  1. reserve `--kv-reserve-tokens` (default 8192) of KV;
  2. experts greedily take the rest, clamped to [floor, total];
  3. KV gets the remainder.

  The floor is `2*num_experts` if prefill overlap is on, else `num_experts` (`engine/cache_budget.py:48-95`; `docs/cli.md:85-86`).
- **Runtime resize without restart:** `OffloadMoeCache.rebuild`, reached through `ft ctl cache --moe N / --kv N` (`offload_cache.py:465-534`; `docs/cli.md:146`).
- **No predictive prefetch across layers in decode.** Experts are fetched on demand, at the layer, after routing. The only look-ahead is in prefill (next-layer full copy) and for PLE rows (the table gather starts before layer 0: `ple.py:580-586`).
- **Instrumentation** is device-side and graph-safe:
  - per-layer miss rates (`offload_cache.py:219-251, 928-977`);
  - an "oracle hit rate" routing-skew analysis (`offload_cache.py:979-1009`).

  **Port this.** It is the cheapest way to size our cache.

### 2.3 Decode, `cpu` and `hybrid` (compute misses on CPU)

- **`cpu`:** the routed experts of CPU layers run in a C++ worker pool reading the host banks. Only activations cross PCIe (`layers/moe.py:271-275`; `moe/cpu_executor.py:1-15`). The decode chain is graph-captured:
  1. D2H of hidden, ids and weights into pinned memory;
  2. submit host node;
  3. sync host node;
  4. H2D of the result.
- **`hybrid`, the paper's q* policy:**
  - `ensure_experts_hybrid` fetches only `F` of the `m` misses. The CPU computes the rest, overlapped with the GPU fetch and GEMM, and the partial outputs are summed (`layers/moe.py:295-339`).
  - `F` is bandwidth-matched: `F ~ m * B_pcie/B_cpu`, rounded to minimize `max(F*(1-q), (m-F)*q)`. It is computed in-kernel in Q16 fixed point (`moe/offload_kernels.py:43-60, 345-355`).
  - Which misses get fetched is decided by **per-expert recency**: recently active experts are fetched first, so recurring misses become resident (`offload_kernels.py:10-16, 361-410`).
  - GPU-assigned routes get CPU id -1, and CPU-assigned routes get GPU weight 0, so every route is computed exactly once (`layers/moe.py:305-339`).
- **Calibration.** `ft bench bw` measures CPU STREAM bandwidth, linear PCIe bandwidth, the real CPU MoE GEMV bandwidth and the real gather-kernel bandwidth, plus both concurrently. It writes `~/.cache/freetoken/benchbw/<gpu-uuid>.json` (`moe/benchbw.py:1-30`; `docs/cli.md:185-203`). Auto picks hybrid only if CPU bandwidth is at least 2x PCIe (`docs/cli.md:202`; `engine/engine.py:1618-1659`).
- **GPU/CPU handshake.** The default flag-sync uses `cuStreamWriteValue64` / `cuStreamWaitValue64` on mapped pinned flags, polled by a persistent CPU coordinator. This replaces `cudaLaunchHostFunc`, which costs ~30-50 us x 2 per layer (~6 ms/step on 75 layers), and avoids spin kernels that fake 99% utilization and trigger power throttling (`moe/cpu_executor.py:33-54`).
- **`--moe-cpu-layers`:** per-layer CPU decode. `auto` picks head and tail layers because "per-layer decode miss rates are U-shaped" (`engine/engine.py:1355-1358`; `docs/cli.md:88`).

### 2.4 CPU kernels

Source: `python/freetoken/kernel/csrc/cpu_moe/cpu_moe_ext.cpp`.

- **Formats:** `WF_BF16`, `WF_NVFP4`, `WF_MXFP4`, `WF_DSFP4`, `WF_Q4_0` (`cpu_moe_ext.cpp:1223`; `cpu_executor.py:73`). **FP8 experts cannot run on CPU** (`docs/cli.md:88`), so Qwen3.8-FP8 in FreeToken is offload-only.
- **ISA ladder**, picked once at construction: AVX-512-BF16 dpbf16 -> AVX-512F widening -> AVX2+FMA -> scalar (`cpu_moe_ext.cpp:13-16, 112-220`). There is an orthogonal W4A8 int8 path using AVX-VNNI or AVX-512-VNNI `vpdpbusd` for nvfp4 and q4_0, where activations are pre-quantized to Q8_0 as in llama.cpp (`:407-565, 1107-1220`).
- **Execution model:**
  - bs=1 GEMV tiled by output rows (IBLK/HBLK=32); each weight byte is read once per token;
  - FP32 accumulate, bf16 intermediate;
  - one pinned thread per physical core, with SMT avoided (`cpu_moe_ext.cpp:1088-1106`; `cpu_executor.py:88-140`).
- **Quoted numbers:** "~205 GB/s vs ~55 GB/s PCIe" on Sapphire Rapids 8480+ with 13 cores (`:1094-1095`); 134 -> 167 GB/s on Emerald Rapids from software prefetch (`:534`).
- **Explicitly deferred:** AMX, expert dedup for bs>1, and NUMA (`:1096-1104`).
- **The CPU is decode-only.** Prefill always runs on the GPU. CPU layers prefill through a synchronous pageable whole-layer copy (`offload_cache.py:1015-1026`).
- **On our host `[inf]`:** the EPYC 7443P is Zen3 with AVX2+FMA only (no AVX-512, no AVX-VNNI). FreeToken would run its AVX2 tier there, e.g. the Q4_0 `maddubs` path (`:1159-1183`).

### 2.5 Prefill strategy

- **Full-layer streaming.** Prefill ignores routing for data movement. It streams **every expert of layer l+1** into one of two full-layer double buffers carved from the first `2*num_experts` slots of the slot cache, while layer l computes (`layers/moe.py:341-397`; `offload_cache.py:606-700, 818-841`).
  - A dedicated copy stream uses ready/release events.
  - A begin-of-prefill fence prevents clobbering slots that an in-flight decode GEMM is reading (`offload_cache.py:645-667`).
- **Why it works:** per chunk (`--max-prefill-length`, default 8192: `docs/cli.md:47`), transfer cost is fixed at the total expert bytes. Throughput is therefore `chunk_tokens * B_pcie / expert_pool_bytes` once compute is hidden.
- **Paper numbers:** an 8192-token chunk of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B bf16 (64.4 GB of experts) on an RTX 5090 took 1.19-1.22 s, matching 52.7 GB/s PCIe5. That is 6.7k tok/s at 16k. Disabling overlap cost 19-26%.
- **`--moe-prefill-hit-d2d`** (opt-in, CUDA 13):
  - experts already resident in the slot cache (slot >= 2E) are gathered device-to-device into the buffer;
  - only the misses cross PCIe, as one `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` of coalesced expert-id runs (`offload_cache.py:746-816`).
  - Driver quirk found empirically: batch memcpy turns **synchronous** when entries under ~256 KB are mixed with large ones on registered memory. Small banks are therefore shipped as one whole-layer entry (`offload_cache.py:17-26`).
- **Fallback.** Without overlap (cache < 2E slots): `materialize_layer`, then a synchronous copy (`layers/moe.py:372-383`).

### 2.6 Pinned buffers and load path

Source: `python/freetoken/moe/host_banks.py`.

- **Pin-after-fill.** Allocate a lazy anonymous mmap, fill it from disk, then `cudaHostRegister(Portable|Mapped)`. Registering first would fault and zero-fill every page (137 GiB -> ~47 s for DSV4) (`host_banks.py:1-16, 78-144`; `kernel/csrc/pinned_tensor.cpp:97-103`).
- **`PinPipeline`** registers finished layers on a background thread while other layers are still being read. `cudaHostRegister` is driver-serialized, so load time is about max(read, pin) (`host_banks.py:286-348`).
- **Exact-size `cudaHostAlloc`** avoids torch's power-of-two pinned rounding: "a 70GB bank would reserve 128GB" (`kernel/pinned.py:1-6`; `pinned_tensor.cpp:46-72`).
- **Parallel reads.** Chunked (8 MiB) multi-threaded O_DIRECT `preadv` into page-aligned banks, with a bounce buffer for unaligned safetensors offsets and `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` beforehand (`host_banks.py:382-473`).
- **FTW format:** a pre-repacked bank layout for direct I/O (`checkpoint/ftw.py`; `docs/cli.md:170-183`). The benchmark `benchmarks/bench_load_weight_generic.py` compares serial vs parallel O_DIRECT vs FTW.

### 2.7 PLE / disk row store (commit f5b9700) - our engram table

There are two backends. `--ple-backend disk` is the **default** (`engine/config.py:33-34`; `server/args.py:618-626`). `docs/models.md:62` still says "pinned" and is stale.

**`pinned` (`PinnedUVATable`):**

- Loads the whole 47.7 GiB table into one pinned HostBank.
- A Triton kernel with **one program per row** (1 warp, latency-bound) gathers rows by UVA directly from host memory, dequantizes fp8 to bf16 with the scalar scale, and writes into a GPU staging buffer (`models/qwen4_exp/ple.py:120-210`; `kernel/triton/ple.py:24-60`).
- `prefetch` launches the gather on a side stream at the top of the forward, so it overlaps layer 0 (`ple.py:580-586`).

**`disk` (`DiskRowTable`, the C++ `RowStore`/`PleStore`)** (`models/qwen4_exp/ple_disk.py`; `kernel/row_store.py`; `kernel/csrc/row_store/row_store_ext.cpp`):

- **No copy.** It maps the checkpoint's `ngram_embedding.shard_<i>` tensors in place as extents (`ple_disk.py:59-95`).
- **Host-side hashing:** the n-gram splitmix hash is ported to C++ so a fill never crosses into Python per row (`row_store_ext.cpp:598-643`).
- **Reads:** each row is read as its 4 KiB-aligned page span with `O_DIRECT` (buffered fallback with `FADV_RANDOM` / `DONTNEED`) (`:130-169, 522-540`).
  - The backend is **io_uring**: raw syscalls, a single issuer, 64 entries, pipelined refill (`:288-417`).
  - Fallback is a 16-thread pread pool ("fio: pread saturates at ~16 threads") (`:48-52, 186-286`).
  - Duplicate rows in one fill are deduped. **There is no RAM cache and no cross-step state** (`:1-4, 522-586`).
- **Graph sync:**
  - The captured decode graph contains `cuStreamWaitValue64(flag>=1)` followed by a reset.
  - The host reads back the sampled token, runs the disk fill into pinned staging, then release-stores the flag. The graph therefore launches before the disk read and stalls only at the PLE consume point (`ple_disk.py:160-238`; `row_store_ext.cpp:66-108`).
  - The fallback is launch-gating: fill before replay.
- **Consume:** the lookup is a fixed-shape H2D copy plus fp8->bf16 dequant (`ple_disk.py:242-261`).
- **Prefill fills are synchronous** on the engine thread before dispatch (`ple_disk.py:221-229`).
- **Constraint:** exactly one PLE layer (`models/qwen4_exp/model.py:176-177`).
- **What f5b9700 changed:** it made `RowStore` hash-agnostic (`stage_rows(row_ids)` + `flush()`), with `PleStore` as a subclass. This is exactly the generic "fixed-width rows from checkpoint files by id" primitive we need.

### 2.8 Other overlap

- "Overlap token limits" (cee23bf) is about **overlap scheduling**, i.e. CPU scheduling running one step ahead of the GPU. It is not about transfers. The fix counts delivered tokens correctly when `device_len` runs ahead (`scheduler/scheduler.py:352`), and zero-inits slot caches so inactive hybrid routes read finite values (`offload_cache.py:357`).
- The copy/compute overlap mechanisms are §2.5 (prefill double buffer), §2.3 (hybrid CPU/GPU concurrency) and §2.7 (PLE prefetch stream and memop wait).

### CPU-side compute on trellis experts (the q* branch)

- **FreeToken's CPU path only handles formats that decode cheaply per element:**
  - bf16 shift;
  - e2m1 LUT via `vpermps`/`vpermd`;
  - Q4_0 nibble + int8 dot.

  FP8 block experts are refused on CPU (`docs/cli.md:88`). The CPU only wins when its GEMV bandwidth is at least 2x PCIe (`benchbw.py:15-19`).
- **EXL3 trellis on CPU `[inf]`:**
  - It requires a per-weight codebook decode (3INST/MCG/MUL1: LCG/hash on a sliding 16-bit state, a handful of integer ops per weight). It also needs input/output Hadamard transforms (cheap: O(n log n) on 128-blocks).
  - On a Zen3 7443P (24 cores, AVX2 only, ~150 GB/s DDR4-3200 x8), the kernel would be **compute-bound**, not bandwidth-bound. A rough estimate is 10-40 G weights/s. The bytes being small (3 bpw) does not help, because the decode ALU cost is per weight.
  - A decode miss set of ~100-200 experts x 4.9 M weights = 0.5-1 G weights/token, so ~25-100 ms/token. **That is too slow to beat PCIe**, which moves 200 x 1.9 MB = 0.38 GB in ~15 ms.
- **If a CPU branch is ever wanted,** do what FreeToken does for other formats: give the CPU a CPU-friendly format. With 503 GB of RAM we can keep a **second host copy of the experts in Q4_0/Q8_0 or int4-g128** (~70-90 GB) just for CPU compute.
  - Caveat: CPU-computed routes would then use a different quantization than the GPU trellis routes. This is not bit-identical and needs a KLD check.
  - Before doing this, run the per-layer miss stats (item 6) and the analog of `ft bench bw` for our kernels.
- **Recommendation:** GPU-only offload (items 1-3) meets the targets on paper. Skip q* at first.

### B70 / Arc notes `[inf]`

- Nothing in FreeToken runs on XPU. The portable parts are the designs, not the code:
  - host-mapped zero-copy gather needs USM host allocations (`zeMemAllocHost` / `sycl::malloc_host`), which the device can dereference over PCIe;
  - the double-buffer streams map to in-order SYCL queues with events;
  - CUDA graphs have no mature equivalent in PyTorch-XPU, so expect higher per-layer launch overhead in decode.
- The trellis GEMM on Battlemage is our own kernel either way.

Each layer has `attn_hyper_connection` and `mlp_hyper_connection`, each with `input_mix_weight_down [320,10240]`, `input_mix_weight_up [10240,320]`, `block_inject_weight [4,10240]` and `hc_norm [10240]`, all **fp16, unquantized**. The final `hyper_connection_mixer` collapses the streams before lm_head. There is no final norm |
| Vocab | `vocab_size: 248320`, `tie_word_embeddings: false` | embed_tokens bf16 `[248320,2560]` is unquantized. lm_head is 5 bpw |
| Context | `max_position_embeddings: 262144` | The card says it extends to 1M with YaRN |
| Vision | 27-block ViT, `hidden_size 1152` | `vision_bits: 5`. Optional for text-only use |

### N-gram embedding (PLE, "per-layer embedding")

Config: `ngram_size: 3`, `heads_per_ngram: 8`, `ngram_vocab_size_base: 20000000`, `split_ngram_parts: 128`, `make_ngram_vocab_size_divisible_by: 128`, `ple_embed_dim: 2560`, `ple_layer_ids: [2]` (1-based per `qwen4_exp.py`, so the tensor key is `layers.1.ple`), `ple_conv_kernel_size: 4`.

- **Heads:** (ngram_size-1) x heads_per_ngram = 2 x 8 = **16 hash heads**. Heads 0-7 hash bigrams and heads 8-15 hash trigrams. Each head has its own table of prime size (`head_vocab_sizes` = 20000003, 20000023, ... 20000171, sum 320,001,446) at `head_offsets` 0, 20000003, ...
- **Table:** `ngram_embedding.safetensors` holds 128 shards `shard_k.trellis`, each `[2500012, 51]` int16. That is **320,001,536 rows** (padded to a multiple of 128) x `row_dim: 160`. File metadata: `format: exl3_ngram_trellis`, `K: 5`, `codebook: mul1`, `row_dim: 160`. Each row is 51 int16 = **102 B**: 160 values x 5 bits = 800 bits = 50 words, plus 1 extra word (`K = (words-1)*16/160`). A per-head fp16 `head_bias [16,160]` is added on dequant. Table bytes: **32,640,162,072 B (32.64 GB)**. The original bf16 table is 320M x 160 x 2 B = 102.4 GB (the "51B" = 51.2B params).
- **Indexing** (`compute_ngram_ids` / `ngram_hash_cpu` in `ngram.cu`): the hash uses shifted token ids t0 (current), t-1 and t-2. Tokens are shifted with eos-segmentation, so an n-gram never crosses an eos.
  `mixed = t0*m0 XOR t-1*m1 [XOR t-2*m2 for trigrams]`, with `layer_multipliers` = [23703573157769, 20109073645365, 8052911324071] (uint64 wrap).
  `row = (mixed mod head_vocab_size[h]) + head_offset[h]`.
  This is a multiplicative-XOR hash modulo a per-head prime. It runs on the CPU and dedups rows per batch.
- **Per token:** **16 rows** are looked up, **once**, at one layer only (PLE layer, 1-based layer 2), not per layer. 16 x 160 = 2560-d feature. That is 16 x 102 = **1,632 B per token** of packed table data (bf16 source: 5,120 B).
- **Use** (`ple.py`): the 2560-d n-gram vector goes to `key_proj [10240,2560]` (one key per stream) and `value_proj [2560,2560]` (shared value). Each stream's normed activation gates the value through a signed-sqrt dot-product gate. A depthwise dilated causal conv follows (kernel 4, dilation 3). The result is added to all 4 residual streams.
- **Runtime:** exllamav3 treats the table as **streamed from disk by default** (`ngram_stream_from_disk`, preads into pinned staging, one H2D, GPU trellis dequant). An `--ngram_ram` mode is also available. Code comment: a cold gather is "~90 ms per 4096-token chunk, vs ~5 ms page-cache-warm". Prefill chunks are prefetched on a worker thread. Decode does its 16-row gather inline.

---

## 2. Byte budget (exact, from shard headers plus `quantization_config.json`)

Bits per tensor (from `quantization_config.json` `bits_per_weight`):

- routed experts: **3**
- QSA indexer `index_qk_proj`: 3
- q/k/v/o, GDN `in_proj_qkv`/`in_proj_z`/`out_proj`, shared expert, lm_head: **5**

Unquantized (fp16/bf16): router, `in_proj_a/b`, all hyper-connection matrices, PLE projections, embed_tokens, and norms/conv/A_log/dt_bias. MTP experts are 3 bpw (`mtp_bits: 3`). The sum of all 7 shards is 52,292,914,076 B. The index `total_size` is 52,358,593,436, which is 65,679,360 B higher, exactly the PLE projections, so it appears to count them twice.

| Category | Bytes | GB | Per layer |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Routed experts (48 x 512)** | **45,770,637,312** | **45.771** | 953,554,944 B (0.954 GB) |
| GDN linear attn (36 layers) | 1,320,448,176 | 1.320 | 36,679,116 |
| Hyper-connections (96 sites + final mixer) | 1,281,249,280 | 1.281 | 26,419,200 (fp16) |
| embed_tokens (bf16) | 1,271,398,400 | 1.271 | - |
| lm_head (5 bpw) | 397,813,764 | 0.398 | - |
| Full attn QSA (12 layers) | 374,280,384 | 0.374 | 31,190,032 |
| Shared expert + gate | 148,623,936 | 0.149 | 3,096,332 |
| Router (fp16) | 125,829,120 | 0.126 | 2,621,440 |
| PLE projections (key/value/conv/norms) | 65,679,360 | 0.066 | once |
| QSA indexer | 7,455,792 | 0.007 | 621,316 |
| MTP routed experts (512) | 953,554,944 | 0.954 | - |
| MTP other + mixer patch | 70,548,008 + 13,127,680 | 0.084 | - |
| Vision | 505,395,600 | 0.505 | - |
| **N-gram table** (separate file) | **32,640,162,072** | **32.640** | once |

(a) **Non-expert text core that must be resident on the GPU** (GDN + HC + QSA + indexer + shared + router + PLE projs + lm_head): **3,721,379,812 B = 3.721 GB**. Adding embed_tokens gives 4,992,778,212 B (4.993 GB). embed_tokens is a 5,120 B/token row gather and can stay on the CPU. Note that 1.28 GB of fp16 hyper-connection weights is **34% of the core** and is read on every token.

(b) **Per routed expert:** 3 projections x (trellis 614,400 B + suh/svh 6,400 B + mul1 4 B) = **1,862,412 B**. That covers 4,915,200 weights at 3.031 bits/weight including scales. The value is identical for all 24,576 experts. **Per layer:** 512 x 1,862,412 = 953,554,944 B. **Total:** 45.771 GB.
Decode touches 10 x 48 = 480 experts per token: **B_act = 893,957,760 B ≈ 0.894 GB/token**. With MTP drafting: +10 x 1,862,412 = 18.6 MB per MTP step.

(c) **N-gram table:** 32.640 GB total, **1,632 B/token** read (16 rows x 102 B). A worst-case NVMe fetch is 16 x 4 KiB pages = 64 KiB/token.

---

## 3. KV cache and recurrent state

Full-attention KV per token = 12 layers x 2 (K,V) x 2 kv heads x 256 x bytes/elem:

- fp16: **24,576 B/token** (fp8: 12,288 B/token)
- QSA indexer key cache **[A]**: one 128-d key per 4-token block per layer, which is 12 x 128 x 2 B / 4 = **768 B/token** (fp16)
- MTP layer, if used, adds +2,048 B/token (fp16)

| Context | KV fp16 | KV fp8 | Indexer keys | Total fp16 / fp8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 200,000 | 4.915 GB | 2.458 GB | 0.154 GB | 5.069 / 2.611 GB |
| 262,144 | 6.442 GB (6.00 GiB) | 3.221 GB (3.00 GiB) | 0.201 GB | 6.644 / 3.423 GB |

Constant per-sequence state:

- GDN recurrent state: 36 x 48 value heads x 128 x 128 x 4 B (fp32) = **113,246,208 B (108 MiB)**
- GDN conv state: 36 x 10240 x 3 x 2 B = 2,211,840 B
- PLE conv state: 10240 x 9 x 2 B = 184,320 B (plus 2 token ids)
- total ≈ **115.6 MB per sequence, independent of length**

---

## 4. Feasibility: 1x RTX 3090 and 1x Arc Pro B70

Assumptions:

- **[A]** runtime context + allocator slack 0.75 GiB
- **[A]** decode workspace 1.0 GiB
- **[A]** VRAM of 24 GiB (3090) and 32 GiB (B70)
- **[A]** PCIe H2D of 25 GB/s practical on both cards. The B70 host slot is PCIe 4.0
- **[A]** EXL3 kernels are CUDA-only today. The B70 numbers are bandwidth bounds that assume a working XPU/SYCL port of the trellis GEMM
- **[A]** decode KV reads: QSA reads the KV of the 2048 selected tokens per layer, and the indexer reads all compressed keys

### 4.1 What fits (text-only, no vision, no MTP, 200k context)

| GPU | KV | embed on GPU | Resident (core + KV + state) | Free for expert cache | Expert slots | Slots/layer | Uniform-routing hit rate |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3090 | fp16 | yes | 10.177 GB | 13.714 GB | 7,363 | 153.4 | 0.300 |
| 3090 | fp16 | no | 8.906 GB | 14.985 GB | 8,046 | 167.6 | 0.327 |
| 3090 | fp8 | yes | 7.719 GB | 16.171 GB | 8,682 | 180.9 | 0.353 |
| 3090 | **fp8** | **no** | **6.448 GB** | **17.443 GB** | **9,365** | **195.1** | **0.381** |
| B70 | fp16 | yes | 10.177 GB | 22.304 GB | 11,975 | 249.5 | 0.487 |
| B70 | **fp8** | **no** | **6.448 GB** | **26.033 GB** | **13,977** | **291.2** | **0.569** |

Formulas:

- `slots = floor(free / 1,862,412)`
- `free = VRAM - ctx - ws - core - [embed] - KV(200k) - state`
- Uniform hit rate = slots_per_layer / 512. This is a pessimistic floor. Real MoE routing is skewed and temporally local, so LRU/LFU hit rates should be higher. **Unmeasured**: this needs routing traces.
- At 262k context, fp16 KV costs 1.57 GB more than at 200k, which is about 845 fewer slots.

For a sense of scale: all routed experts (45.77 GB) never fit. Only 38% (3090) or 57% (B70) of them fit even in the best configuration.

### 4.2 Decode bound

Per-token GPU bytes = core 3.721 GB + active experts 0.894 GB + indexer keys 0.154 GB + selected KV 0.050 GB + GDN state read/write 0.231 GB = **5.050 GB**. The weight-bandwidth ceilings are therefore:

- 3090: 936/5.050 = **185 tok/s**
- B70: 608/5.050 = **120 tok/s**

These assume 100% bandwidth efficiency. Real efficiency is lower.

PCIe miss traffic per token = `(1-h) x 10 x 48 x 1,862,412 = (1-h) x 0.894 GB`. Throughput:

- no overlap: `tok/s = 1 / (5.050e9/BW_gpu + (1-h)*0.894e9/25e9)`
- perfect overlap: `tok/s = 1 / max(...)`

| Hit rate h | Miss MB/token | PCIe-only bound | 3090 serial / overlap | B70 serial / overlap |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.00 | 894.0 | 28.0 | 24.3 / 28.0 | 22.7 / 28.0 |
| 0.25 | 670.5 | 37.3 | 31.0 / 37.3 | 28.5 / 37.3 |
| 0.381 (3090 uniform) | 553.4 | 45.2 | **36.3 / 45.2** | - |
| 0.50 | 447.0 | 55.9 | 43.0 / 55.9 | 38.2 / 55.9 |
| 0.569 (B70 uniform) | 385.3 | 64.9 | - | **42.2 / 64.9** |
| 0.75 | 223.5 | 111.9 | 69.8 / 111.9 | 58.0 / 111.9 |
| 0.90 | 89.4 | 279.7 | 111.5 / 185.3 | 84.2 / 120.4 |
| 0.95 | 44.7 | 559.3 | 139.2 / 185.3 | 99.1 / 120.4 |

The router of layer L is known only after that layer's attention, so a miss stalls unless it is predicted ahead. The serial column is the realistic figure without a predictor. One layer's misses at h=0 are 10 x 1.86 MB = 18.6 MB, which takes 0.745 ms at 25 GB/s.

**CPU experts instead of PCIe** (EPYC 7443P, 8ch DDR4-3200, practical 150-190 GB/s):

- Weight bytes per token by format:
  - EXL3 3.03 bpw: 0.894 GB, giving **168-213 tok/s** (bandwidth bound)
  - Q4 at about 4.5 bpw (a second copy of about 68 GB in RAM): 1.327 GB, giving **113-143 tok/s**
  - Q8 at about 8.5 bpw: 2.507 GB, giving **60-76 tok/s**
- Only 5 KB/token/layer of activations crosses PCIe.
- **[A]** EXL3 trellis decode on the CPU is compute-heavy: 2.36 G weights/token must be decoded. Expect it to be compute-bound well below the bandwidth bound. It has not been measured.
- Hybrid (GPU runs cache hits, CPU runs misses, no weight transfer) at the 3090 uniform h=0.381: CPU miss bytes 0.553 GB take 2.9-3.7 ms against 5.4 ms of GPU time. That gives 110-120 tok/s serial and up to 185 tok/s overlapped (bandwidth bounds). This dominates PCIe streaming for decode.

### 4.3 Prefill bound (expert streaming)

A chunk of N tokens leaves a given expert untouched with probability `P = (1-10/512)^N`:

- N=256: P = 0.0064
- N=2048: P = 2.9e-18

So from about 256 tokens up, **every expert of every layer is touched**. Per-chunk PCIe cost = (45.771 GB - cached expert bytes) / 25 GB/s. Streaming also needs a double-buffered per-layer staging area of 2 x 0.954 = 1.907 GB, taken out of the cache. `tok/s = N / t_chunk`.

| Cached experts on GPU | Streamed GB/chunk | s/chunk | 2k | 4k | 8k | 16k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 45.771 | 1.831 | 1,119 | 2,237 | 4,474 | 8,949 |
| 3090 (15.54 GB after staging) | 30.235 | 1.209 | 1,693 | 3,387 | 6,774 | 13,547 |
| B70 (24.13 GB after staging) | 21.645 | 0.866 | 2,365 | 4,731 | 9,462 | 18,924 |

These are PCIe-only bounds. **[A]** Compute bound: about 6B active params means about 12 GFLOP/token. On the 3090 at 71 TFLOPS fp16 (fp32 accumulate), a 30-40% kernel efficiency gives roughly 1,800-2,400 tok/s. So at 4k+ chunks the 3090 is compute-bound, not PCIe-bound, and PCIe only binds at 2k chunks. Also **[A]** activation workspace grows with N: the fp32 4-stream residual alone is 40,960 B/token, which is 671 MB per buffer at 16k.

### 4.4 N-gram table: RAM vs NVMe

- **Capacity:** 503 GB RAM holds everything with room to spare: experts 45.8 GB + n-gram table 32.6 GB + the rest ~6 GB = ~85 GB. Even the bf16 source table (102.4 GB) fits. **An NVMe tier is not needed for capacity**, only as an explicit design requirement. Because exllamav3's default mode streams from disk via pread, with 503 GB RAM the file stays in page cache after first touch anyway.
- **RAM lookup:** 16 random gathers of 102 B each, about 1.6 KB/token. Negligible: microseconds per token, and a 16k prefill chunk is 26 MB of H2D.
- **NVMe (990 Pro, ~1M IOPS random 4K):**
  - Decode: 16 reads/token. Only about 2.5% of rows straddle a 4 KiB page (101/4096). The IOPS ceiling is 62,500 tok/s, but latency is about 80-100 µs per token for a QD16 burst **[A]**. It is issued at step start, since the ids are known before layer 1, and overlaps layer 0.
  - Prefill: 16 x 16,384 = 262,144 reads per 16k chunk, or 0.26 s at 1M IOPS. That is below the 0.87-1.83 s expert-streaming time, so it is not the bottleneck if prefetched. Read amplification is about 40x (4 KiB per 102 B row).
- **GPU residency of the table:** impossible on either card (32.6 GB), and pointless given its 1.6 KB/token traffic.

### Bottom line

Resident core ≈ 3.7 GB plus KV (2.5-4.9 GB at 200k). That leaves 17.4 GB (3090) or 26.0 GB (B70) of expert cache: 38% or 57% of all experts. Decode with PCIe expert streaming is bounded at about 36-45 tok/s (3090) and 42-65 tok/s (B70) at uniform-routing hit rates. CPU-side miss compute (no weight transfer) raises the bound to about 110-185 tok/s, subject to the unmeasured CPU trellis-decode speed. Prefill is PCIe-bound at about 1.1-1.7k tok/s for 2k chunks and becomes compute-bound (about 2k tok/s on the 3090) from 4-8k chunks up. The n-gram table belongs in RAM or page cache. NVMe is optional.

Unlock datacenter-class intelligence on the hardware you already own — Run 290B+ frontier MoE models locally on your gaming PC at blistering interactive speeds. ## About FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving engine designed for running frontier-scale open-weight models on personal and consumer hardware. It treats heterogeneous edge resources—GPUs, CPUs, host memory, and interconnects—as a unified, elastic inference platform. Its core features include: - **Fast Edge-Native Runtime**: Provides efficient MoE serving with bandwidth-adaptive CPU–GPU co-execution ($q^\star$ policy), full-layer double-buffered prefill streaming, global LRU expert caching, graph-compatible execution, and the FTW fast weight format. - **Semantic-Aware Caching**: Features semantic anchor checkpoints for recurrent state and KV caches, allowing agentic context edits (e.g., tool calls, thinking blocks) to avoid redundant context recomputation. - **Elastic Memory Management**: Supports dynamic, runtime VRAM re-allocation between expert caches and KV memory without engine restarts or weight reloading. - **Broad MoE & Ecosystem Support**: Supports frontier open-weight MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, GLM-5.2) across various parameter scales and quantization formats (e.g., MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8, BF16), with Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible APIs for seamless integration with real-world coding and tool-calling agents (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness). - **Diverse Consumer Hardware**: Scales across consumer laptops, gaming desktops, and workstation GPUs, with native support for NVIDIA RTX 30, RTX 40, and RTX 50 series GPUs. ## Getting Started ### Desktop app Download FreeToken for Windows or Linux at [flashml.ai](https://www.flashml.ai/). It sets the engine up for you and gives you a GUI for running models, chatting, and tuning the engine.
### CLI Install FreeToken with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (recommended) or pip: ```bash uv pip install "freetoken[accel]" ``` Or build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken.git && cd FreeToken uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e ".[accel]" ``` For More details: - [Install FreeToken](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/install.md) - [Quick start](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md) - [Supported models](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/models.md) - [CLI reference](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/cli.md) - [Repairing old FTW checkpoints](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/ftw-hotfix.md) ## Citation If you use FreeToken for your research, please cite our [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16157): ```bibtex @article{yang2026freetoken, title={FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution}, author={Yang, Shuo and Fan, Xiaoze and Pan, Melissa and Xi, Haocheng and Wang, Zhe and Sun, Shanlin and Keutzer, Kurt and Han, Song and Zaharia, Matei and Xu, Chenfeng and Stoica, Ion}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.16157}, year={2026} } ``` ## Acknowledgment FreeToken was deeply inspired by [mini-sglang](https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang), and learned the design and reused code from the following projects: [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang), [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), [FlashInfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer), [flash-linear-attention](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention), [LightLLM](https://github.com/ModelTC/lightllm) and [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp). ## License [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/LICENSE). # CLI reference ``` ft [args] ``` | Command | Purpose | |---|---| | `ft serve` | Start the API server (OpenAI `/v1/*`, Anthropic `/v1/messages`, Responses) | | `ft shell` | Chat with a server in the terminal | | `ft ctl` | Query and manage a running server over HTTP | | `ft launch` | Configure and launch a coding agent against a server | | `ft checkpoint` | Convert an HF checkpoint to the FTW fast-load format | | `ft bench bw` | Benchmark CPU vs PCIe bandwidth to calibrate the MoE backend | `ft --version` prints the installed version (torch-free; nightly wheels carry a `+g` build stamp, tagged releases a bare version). Every command supports `--help`. ## ft serve ```bash ft serve --model [options] ``` `--model` is the only required flag — dtype, attention backend, MoE backend, MoE cache size, KV capacity, CUDA-graph sizes and the tool-call/reasoning parsers all resolve automatically from the checkpoint and the GPU. ### Model | Flag | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `--model-path`, `--model` | required | Local dir, HF repo id, or an FTW dir (auto-detected) | | `--served-model-name` | basename of `--model` | Model id reported by `/v1/models` | ### Server & runtime | Flag | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `--host` | 127.0.0.1 | Bind address | | `--port` | 1919 | Bind port | | `--gpu` | GPU 0 | GPU to run on: a UUID from `nvidia-smi -L` or an `nvidia-smi` index; see [below](#choosing-a-gpu) | | `--max-running-requests` | 4 | Max concurrently running requests | | `--max-output-tokens` | 32768 | Default output budget for requests that omit one | | `--max-seq-len-override` | from checkpoint | Max sequence length | | `--max-prefill-length` | 8192 | Chunked-prefill chunk size in tokens | | `--cuda-graph-max-bs`, `--graph` | = max running requests | Max batch size captured as CUDA graphs | | `--decode-log-interval` | 40 | Scheduler status line every N decode steps | ### Choosing a GPU For example, a machine with an RTX 5090 and an RTX 3060 Ti: ```console $ nvidia-smi -L GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (UUID: GPU-2f3a9b1c-8d7e-4a05-b6c1-0e5f9a3d7b42) GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (UUID: GPU-9e8d7c6b-5a49-4f13-8207-c1b0a4e6d3f5) ``` ```bash ft serve --model ... --gpu 1 # by nvidia-smi index -- the 5090 ft serve --model ... --gpu GPU-9e8d7c6b # the same card by UUID (a unique prefix is enough) ``` ### KV cache & memory | Flag | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `--memory-ratio` | 0.9 | Fraction of free VRAM the engine may use (weights + MoE cache + KV) | | `--num-pages` / `--num-tokens` | auto | KV capacity override in pages / tokens (mutually exclusive; auto sizes from VRAM left after weights and MoE cache) | | `--page-size` | 1 | KV page size; DSV4 forces 128, the TRTLLM backend needs 16/32/64, SWA models require 1 | | `--cache-type` | radix | `radix` (prefix reuse;
